dedupe_keys.name: understanding and quantifying structural loading from tsunami induced debris fields

description: Understanding and Quantifying Structural Loading from Tsunami-Induced Debris Fields is a dataset listed in DesignSafe Data Depot (published projects), a research data repository for natural hazards engineering under the section "experimental", published or maintained by Michael Motley, University of Washington (washington.edu). Tsunamis and storm surges pose a significant threat to coastal communities around the world. In tsunami risk zones, the threats from large-scale coastal inundation are exacerbated by the accumulation of large debris fields that impact and build up around critical infrastructure systems. Coverage: as described in the project (site or event named in the description). DesignSafe files it as a "experimental" project. Keywords: Debris, Waves, Tsunamis, Coastal structure. Published 2024-05-10. It is reached through the links recorded on this page, with the catalogue entry as the discovery route. Access is free of charge and open. The licence is ODC-By-1.0. Caveats: this record was written from the catalogue listing only, so the linked page was not opened, its contents and current availability were not checked, and the description may lag the source. It can support structural performance, hazard exposure and resilience studies. Related record: the catalogue-level record data-designsafe-data-depot-repository.
